intro_flat.text: Dutch calls every day. Dutch calls to tell us the rent is late.
Real work? Like, paying work? Not “hold this bag and don’t look inside” work?
The Drowned Saint. Ten minutes. And eat something first. Nobody punches well on an empty stomach.
Hungry’s fine. Hungry’s how I win.
Rook takes his coat from the hook the slow way, keeping his left side still.
Doc Yun said three weeks off. It’s been one.
Then I’m two weeks ahead. The ribs are fine. It’s the wiring that’s sulking.

first_fight_win.text: Well, well. Rook’s little stray. Nice jacket. Bet it looks better on me.
Bet it looks better on you when you’re not face down in a puddle.
Two Rustfangs. Try not to show off.
Sloppy. You dropped your guard twice.
You beat Rustfangs. That’s like beating the weather. Come on.
He says it with a hand pressed flat to his side, where he thinks she can’t see.

first_fight_lose.text: Well, well. Rook’s little stray. Nice jacket. Bet it looks better on me.
Bet it looks better on you when you’re not face down in a puddle.
Two Rustfangs. Try not to show off.

meet_dutch_first.text: There they are. My favorite disaster and his apprentice. Sit, sit. Mind the stain, it’s load-bearing.
This is Mr. Pale. He represents, let’s say, an interested party.
Mr. Pale is peeling a satsuma with a small folding knife. The peel comes away in one unbroken spiral. He never looks at his hands.
A pleasure. I’ll be brief; I bill by the minute. Under the flooded Sinkline there is a sealed research annex. Kessler-Mori wrote it off after the flood of ’61.
Inside is a {y}data core{/}. Bring it to me intact and you will be paid {y}three thousand cred{/}.
Three thou—
Kit.
A written-off annex. A milk run. You could send anybody. Why us?
Because “anybody” asks more questions. Also, the annex doors are still corporate-locked. You will need a deck jockey.
Which you haven’t got, since your last one moved to Neo-Lagos and stopped taking my calls.
…Hex.
Hex! Hex owes me money. Two birds, one run. Tell them if they do this, their tab goes in the canal.
Expenses. I will not be asking for receipts.
Loading Dock 7, when you have it. I keep very exact hours.
Miss Kit. Those two Rustfangs outside: nine seconds, no weapon, no chrome in those hands. I watched from the window.
So?
So nothing. I collect numbers. That one is unusual.
She’s not part of the price.
Of course not, Mr. Rook. Prices are for things one pays for.
He splits the satsuma, counts the segments under his breath, and leaves it on the table uneaten. He is gone before the door finishes swinging.
Does that every time. Never eats one. Don’t ask.
Word of advice? Get paid before you get proud.
I’m always proud.
I know, darlin’. That’s why I said it to you and not him. Oh, and if you need pocket money, the {c}job board{/} by the door always has something.

meet_dutch_again.text: The meter’s running on Mr. Pale’s patience. Go find your jockey.

meet_dutch_again_sable.text: Whoever that is with you, darlin’, I never saw him. I never saw any of you.

meet_hex_first.text: I didn’t do it. Whatever it is. Oh— it’s you. Hi, Rook. Hi, Rook’s kid.
Kit. My name’s been Kit for nineteen years.
We have a job. Corporate doors, down in the Sinkline.
No. Absolutely not. Also I can’t: my deck’s dead. Fried the coprocessor on an all-nighter. A hobby. Look at her. She’s crying.
With what cred? A Stingray costs more than this building. Which I also owe money on.

Some is a number. I can work with a number. There’s a scavver in the Rustyard, {y}Old Mags{/}. She had a Stingray last month. Rustyard’s east, past the Barrens. Get me that chip and I’m your jockey. Your professional, sober deck jockey.
The Barrens are nasty. Here, I can spare these.

meet_hex_asked.text: Rustyard. Old Mags. Stingray, the one with the little fin logo. I’ll be here. Checking the door locks. Twice.

meet_hex_chip.text: Is that— is that a Stingray? Don’t drop it. Please don’t drop it. Slowly. Give it here slowly.
No. You do it. My hands are shaking. Pins to pins, then the clips. I’ll talk you through it.
Hex’s deck runs a new program: {y}Overload{/}, a surge that fries machines. Their deck’s under {c}Deck{/} in the menu now.
Rook. Sit. Your reflex wiring’s been double-firing since you walked in. I can hear it clicking. Chrome shouldn’t click.
Hex runs a cable from the deck to the port behind Rook’s ear. Thirty seconds of scrolling numbers. Something in his shoulder stops twitching.
Rook’s chrome is re-tuned: {y}Quickdraw{/} and {y}Reflex Burst{/} are back, and his wound costs him less.
Your side’s still a mess, though. That’s meat. I don’t do meat.
Okay. A deal’s a deal. I’m already regretting it. Let’s go rob a haunted subway.
Also, my emergency fund. It’s mostly been emergencies.
One more thing. I run a scanner, {c}Analyze{/}. Feed its target data into Rook’s smartgun and he literally cannot miss. I call it {y}Target Lock{/}. Patent pending.

rustyard_gate_win.text: Off my lot. Forty years I’ve held this yard against worse than you, and I’m still counting.
Knuckles says this yard pays tribute now, grandma. Hounds! Fetch.
Knuckles is gonna hear about this! He’s gonna feed you to the hounds!
Hmph. Didn’t need help. Didn’t mind it, either. What do you want?
Ha! Had one. Knuckles’ boys took it, along with half my stock. Hauled it all up to the old {y}tire depot{/} at the north end of the yard.
You do that and the chip’s yours. Plus a discount at my counter. Deal’s a deal.

rustyard_gate_lose.text: Off my lot. Forty years I’ve held this yard against worse than you, and I’m still counting.
Knuckles says this yard pays tribute now, grandma. Hounds! Fetch.

knuckles_win.text: So these are the heroes. Know what I do to heroes? I charge ’em rent.
Ugh… fine… take your junk… I’m moving to Neo-Lagos…
Your fixer’s got a big mouth, y’know. Whole yard knew you were hunting a deck jockey before you did.
Dutch talks. That’s not the same as selling us.
The crate. Mags’ stuff should be in there.

knuckles_lose.text: So these are the heroes. Know what I do to heroes? I charge ’em rent.

mags_early.text: Tire depot, north end. Knuckles is the big one with the chrome hands. Can’t miss him. Wish I could.

mags_take_stash.text: Well, well. Knuckles is limping all the way to Neo-Lagos, I hear. Here. As promised.
Our water filter was in that crate too. The little ones have been drinking canal for a month.
We found the camp’s tribute as well. Behind the tagged heap. It’s yours.
Keep it. Where you’re going you’ll need it more than we will. The camp voted. I counted.
And this. The camp took up a collection for whoever ran Knuckles off: {y}150¢{/}. Don’t argue with me, I’m old.
And tell Hex they still owe me for the last one.

mags_keep_stash.text: Well, well. Knuckles is limping all the way to Neo-Lagos, I hear. Here. As promised.
Our water filter was in that crate too. The little ones have been drinking canal for a month.
We found the camp’s tribute as well. Behind the tagged heap. It’s yours.
Keep it. Where you’re going you’ll need it more than we will. The camp voted. I counted.
And this. The camp took up a collection for whoever ran Knuckles off: {y}150¢{/}. Don’t argue with me, I’m old.
Keep it. The little ones need it more than our rent does.
Hmph. Then here’s what it buys you: anything on my lot, a fifth off. For as long as I’m breathing.
And tell Hex they still owe me for the last one.

mags_take.text: Well, well. Knuckles is limping all the way to Neo-Lagos, I hear. Here. As promised.
Our water filter was in that crate too. The little ones have been drinking canal for a month.
And this. The camp took up a collection for whoever ran Knuckles off: {y}150¢{/}. Don’t argue with me, I’m old.
And tell Hex they still owe me for the last one.

Our water filter was in that crate too. The little ones have been drinking canal for a month.
And this. The camp took up a collection for whoever ran Knuckles off: {y}150¢{/}. Don’t argue with me, I’m old.

Hmph. Then here’s what it buys you: anything on my lot, a fifth off. For as long as I’m breathing.
And tell Hex they still owe me for the last one.

mags_shop.text: Shopping? The crew that ran Knuckles off my lot gets fair prices. For once.

mags_talk.text: Shopping? The crew that ran Knuckles off my lot gets fair prices. For once.
The Sinkline? Flooded in ’61, whole trains still down there. Things live in the water now. Big things. Bring fire. Or a bigger thing.

mags_leave.text: Shopping? The crew that ran Knuckles off my lot gets fair prices. For once.

sinkline_gate_alone.text: A transit-authority service gate. The lock panel blinks {r}LOCKED{/}: corporate encryption.
This is what the jockey’s for.

sinkline_gate_hex.text: Transit authority lock with Kessler-Mori wrapping. Cute. Give me a second.
Done. Welcome to the Sinkline. Mind the gap. Mind the ghosts. Mind the everything.

dead_crew.text: Three bodies in expensive gear, slumped against the platform. Whatever got them wasn’t a ghoul. Their wounds are cauterized.
That’s the {c}Glass Wolves{/}. Runners out of Harbor Ward. Good ones.
One of them clutches a data slate. The last message reads: {c}“Dutch set it up. Milk run. In and out.”{/}
Same job. Different crew. Before us. And he sat there and poured us drinks and didn’t say a word.
Maybe he didn’t know they didn’t come back.
Dutch knows everything that happens below the canal. That’s what he sells.
A cred stick in the leader’s jacket, still warm with charge.
They’d want it spent on the job that killed them. Take it.

pump_v1_open.text: Intake 1, open. The gauge sits steady at {c}50 psi{/}.

pump_v2_open.text: Intake 2, open. The gauge sits steady at {c}30 psi{/}.

pump_v3_open.text: Intake 3, open. The gauge sits steady at {c}70 psi{/}.

pump_v2_leave_first.text: Hold on. Before anybody cranks a random wheel: this is one of the pump intakes. The pump room console should say how they want opening. South, off the platform.
Intake 2: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}30 psi{/}.

pump_v2_leave_seen.text: Intake 2: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}30 psi{/}.

pump_v2_right_first.text: Intake 2: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}30 psi{/}.
The wheel grinds round. Water hisses into Intake 2, and somewhere across the level a pipe knocks in answer.

pump_v1_right_second.text: Intake 1: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}50 psi{/}.
The wheel grinds round. Water hisses into Intake 1, and somewhere across the level a pipe knocks in answer.

pump_v3_right_last.text: Intake 3: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}70 psi{/}.
The last wheel turns. Every pipe in the room drums once, then settles into a low, even hum.
Pressure’s balanced and the pumps are primed. Now the console in the pump room.

pump_v1_wrong_first_seen.text: Intake 1: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}50 psi{/}.
{r}BANG.{/} A pressure kick hammers down the line. The wheel won’t budge.
Okay. Order matters. Lowest pressure first, and that means reading all three gauges before we touch anything. I did say that. Out loud.

pump_v1_wrong_first_unseen.text: Intake 1: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}50 psi{/}.
{r}BANG.{/} A pressure kick hammers down the line. The wheel won’t budge.
Okay. Order matters. There’s a right order, and the pump console in the pump room knows it. Let’s go ask it.

pump_v3_wrong_after_one.text: Intake 3: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}70 psi{/}.
{r}BANG.{/} A pressure kick hammers down the line, and Intake 2’s wheel spins shut again.

pump_v1_wrong_after_two.text: Intake 1: a rusted valve wheel. Its gauge reads {c}50 psi{/}.
{r}BANG.{/} A pressure kick hammers down the line, and Intake 1’s wheel spins shut again.

floodgate_done.text: The pump console hums. Water levels: {g}NOMINAL{/}.

floodgate_dry_first.text:
The pump console flickers awake: {r}INTAKES DRY.{/} {c}PRIME: OPEN INTAKES 1–3, LOWEST PRESSURE FIRST.{/}
Intake 1: platform track bed · Intake 2: service bay · Intake 3: this station.
Three intakes, all over the level. We read every gauge first. Then we open them lowest to highest. Nobody touches a wheel before that. Please.

floodgate_dry_seen.text:
The pump console flickers awake: {r}INTAKES DRY.{/} {c}PRIME: OPEN INTAKES 1–3, LOWEST PRESSURE FIRST.{/}
Intake 1: platform track bed · Intake 2: service bay · Intake 3: this station.

floodgate_ready.text: Pump control. Still got power, somehow. If I spin up the drainage pumps, the junction should empty out.
And whatever lives in the junction?
Will be a lot easier to see coming. Best I can do from a pump console.
Across the level, pumps groan to life. The black water in the junction falls away, and a catwalk rises out of it.

lurker_win.text: The water— it’s moving on its own.
That is not water. That is a LOT of teeth.
Maintenance shaft past the junction goes down. The annex should be under us.

lurker_lose.text: The water— it’s moving on its own.
That is not water. That is a LOT of teeth.

annex_door_locked.text: A pressure door marked {c}K-M ANNEX 7 · AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL{/}. The lock wants a physical passkey.
Hardware key. I can’t crack a chunk of plastic. Somebody down here has one.

annex_guards_win.text: Contact! Unauthorized personnel in Annex 7! Lethal response authorized!
One of the Sentinels wears a passkey on a lanyard. Hex lifts it off him with two fingers.
One chunk of plastic, acquired. Told you somebody down here had one.
Huh. The door log has us in it. “Contractor team, due the 14th. Status: pending resolution.” That’s a weird word for a door to use.
Active security in an abandoned lab. Pale lied.
Pale lied, the lab lied, the lights are lying. I read systems for a living, and nothing down here will tell me the truth.

annex_guards_lose.text: Contact! Unauthorized personnel in Annex 7! Lethal response authorized!

lattice_first.text:
A security lattice: three emitters, beams humming across the passage. Three cables climb its frame, amber, green and violet, each tapping into some of the emitters.
Emitters: 1 {r}LIVE{/}  ·  2 {r}LIVE{/}  ·  3 {r}LIVE{/}
Can’t hack a laser. But lasers need power, and power comes through relays. Find the relays.

lattice_seen_a.text:
A security lattice: three emitters, beams humming across the passage. Three cables climb its frame, amber, green and violet, each tapping into some of the emitters.
Emitters: 1 {g}DARK{/}  ·  2 {g}DARK{/}  ·  3 {r}LIVE{/}

relay_a_down.text: Relay A (amber cable). The lattice is down; nothing left to route.

relay_b_down.text: Relay B (green cable). The lattice is down; nothing left to route.

relay_c_down.text: Relay C (violet cable). The lattice is down; nothing left to route.

relay_a_leave_first.text: Security relay. I can cycle it, but I can’t see what it feeds from here. Only one way to find out.

relay_b_leave_first.text: Security relay. I can cycle it, but I can’t see what it feeds from here. Only one way to find out.

relay_c_leave_first.text: Security relay. I can cycle it, but I can’t see what it feeds from here. Only one way to find out.

relay_a_cycle.text: The relay clunks over. Lattice emitters: 1 {g}DARK{/}  ·  2 {g}DARK{/}  ·  3 {r}LIVE{/}

relay_c_cycle.text: The relay clunks over. Lattice emitters: 1 {r}LIVE{/}  ·  2 {g}DARK{/}  ·  3 {g}DARK{/}

relay_b_cycle_dark.text: Down the hall, the laser lattice stutters, flickers, and dies.
Lattice is down! Turns out I can lie to a lab too.

relay_b_cycle_first.text: Security relay. I can cycle it, but I can’t see what it feeds from here. Only one way to find out.
Down the hall, the laser lattice stutters, flickers, and dies.
Lattice is down! Turns out I can lie to a lab too.

cryopod_full.text: A cryopod, humming, lit from within. Frost on the glass. Behind it, a figure: an orc, bone-white hair, eyes closed.
Label reads {c}ASSET S-7 · “VESSEL” · SPARK YIELD 94%{/}. Oh no. Oh no no no.
This is the data core. It’s not data. It’s a person.
We’re getting them out.
Kit. Three thousand cred, the rent, Hex’s debt—
Nine seconds. Pale timed me in the street and wrote it down.
That’s how you end up in there, Rook. Somebody likes your numbers.
We’re getting them OUT.
Twenty years ago I stood in a lab like this. Different logo. My crew got paid, and I walked out past a tank with somebody still in it.
I told myself it wasn’t my job. I’ve been telling myself that every night since.
Do it, kid. Whatever it costs.
You never told me that.
You never needed to carry it. Now you do. Go on.
For the record, I hate “whatever it costs.” I’m doing it anyway.
Kit’s hand touches the glass, and something in her answers. Ki surges up through her arm like a struck match. Frost blooms, cracks, and shatters.
…The crow was screaming. For so long. Now it’s quiet.
You. Your hands are burning.
Started last month. I don’t know why.
Mm. The crow says you’re loud. That’s not an insult.
I am Sable. I don’t know how long I was in there. They took— they took a lot. I still have enough.
We’ll get you out of here. After that you owe us nothing.
Everyone who opened this glass said something kind. The crow remembers each of them.
We’re not them.
No. None of them burned.
There were others. S-5. S-6. The pods beside mine went dark, one night and then another. Nobody wrote down where they went.
Somebody did. It’s in the pod logs.
Hex jacks into the pod’s panel. For a long minute the only sound is the deck, copying: intake dates, yields, transfer orders. Every name.
Got it. All of it. It goes wherever we go, and it doesn’t go to Pale.
…Then I will walk with you. As far as the door. After that I will decide.
Hex puts their jacket round Sable’s shoulders. Rook watches the door. Nobody says anything about three thousand cred.
Kit falls in beside Rook. She doesn’t ask about the other tank, and he doesn’t offer. Their shoulders touch, once, on the way to the door.
You. The old one. You’re bleeding under that coat.
Old news.
The crow doesn’t care how old it is. Hold still.
Sable lays two fingers against Rook’s side. Something black-feathered and warm passes through the room. When he steps back, the stitches are just a scar.
Rook’s wound is closed: full strength, every charge back, and {y}Second Wind{/} too.
…Huh.
Don’t get used to it. You still owe Doc Yun for the stitches.
{r}ALERT. ASSET S-7 CONTAINMENT BREACH. WARDEN PROTOCOL ENGAGED.{/}
WARDEN protocol. That sounds big. Things named “Warden” are always big.
Freight lift. South, through the containment door. Move.
One stop first: that armory by the hall had weapon cases. Whatever WARDEN is, I want to meet it holding something better.

warden_win.text: The floor shudders. A security platform unfolds from the wall, three meters of plate and cannon. Something inside its chest glows and screams.
There’s a spirit in its heart. Bound. Starving. It was one of us once.
Then we set it free. Crew, on me.
The spirit rises from the wreck, no longer screaming. It circles Sable once, like a bird, and fades into the pipes.
It thanked you. It said its name. I won’t repeat it; it was only for us.
Not this time. That’s all I wanted.
The crow has gone up the lift shaft ahead of us. It sees farther than I can.
Cars at the top. People waiting in the rain.
Pale’s pickup. He did say he keeps exact hours.
The lift’s live. Let’s never come back here.

warden_lose.text: The floor shudders. A security platform unfolds from the wall, three meters of plate and cannon. Something inside its chest glows and screams.
There’s a spirit in its heart. Bound. Starving. It was one of us once.
Then we set it free. Crew, on me.

betrayal_go_for_pale.text: Mr. Pale is waiting under the cranes, peeling a satsuma. The spiral of peel hangs from his knife, unbroken.
Three minutes early. I do appreciate punctuality in a liability.
Your “property” is a person.
Asset S-7 is Kessler-Mori property, recovered from a site we officially abandoned by deniable contractors.
You were the deniable contractors.
And the three thousand?
A figure of speech.
I did tell you I collect numbers, Miss Kit. I have already sold yours.
He splits the satsuma and counts the segments under his breath. Eleven.
Contractors are paid on completion. You have completed.
Except you, Miss Kit. The Vessel program is always short of subjects.
The peel drops to the wet concrete. One unbroken spiral.
Contractor tags read. Four signatures. One flagged for intake, three for disposal.
Rifles come up all along the dock.
choices: Get in front of Hex and Sable

betrayal_go_for_pale.text: Kit is across the gap before she has decided to be. A Sentinel’s rifle butt meets her halfway, and the concrete meets her after that.
Nine seconds in the street, Miss Kit. You were faster when nobody was watching.
Kit. When I say run, you run. You don’t look back, you don’t wait for me.
Rook’s hand comes out of his coat with something small and round in it. The pin is already gone.
Rook—
Run.

betrayal_cover_crew.text: Kit plants herself in front of Hex and Sable, fists up, burning. The crow screams from a crane. Every red dot on the dock finds her chest.
Touching. Inefficient, but touching.
Kit. When I say run, you run. You don’t look back, you don’t wait for me.
Rook’s hand comes out of his coat with something small and round in it. The pin is already gone.
Rook—
Run.
